findings.claim: The write-target authorization path still depends on the repository read-case path, so the PostgreSQL implementation requires `case:read` for write-only case operations.
findings.evidence: `authorize_case_write_target` checks `case_write` and then calls `self.cases.read_case(context, case_id)`, while `PgGateRepository::read_case` executes `SELECT aso.read_case($1)` and the migration defines `aso.read_case` as `PERFORM aso.require_case(target_case, 'case:read')`; this contradicts the spec scenario requiring refusal only when the caller lacks the capability required by the operation and the accepted resolution that write resources use `case_write` without also requiring `case:read`.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a repository method/SQL function that verifies case existence and tenant scope with `case_write` (for example `aso.require_case(target_case, 'case_write')`) and have `authorize_case_write_target` call that instead of `read_case`.
